answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every newcomer to lock a small bond that peers slash whenever they catch duplicate behavior. Picture the registry as an atlas where each identity must claim one unique, costly coordinate, like a lone mesa rising from flat desert: easy to survey, hard to fake twice. Because the bond is ferrous, sticking like iron to a public work history, spinning up a thousand puppets means posting a thousand bonds, so an attack costs more than it can ever earn.
